subject: bug in y-axis scaling for small values

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: bug in y-axis scaling for small values
parts:
Dear list,

I was quite puzzled to see an horizontal line in my graph today, until
I realised that it was a ggplot2 bug. The data were definitely not
constant, but small (around 1e-10 with some dispersion). Base plots
don't have any trouble finding the range of this data, and it's
clearly not a case of numerical accuracy either. Consider this minimal
example,

library(ggplot2)

set.seed(123)
d1 <- d2 <- data.frame(x=seq(0,10, length=1e2),
y=rnorm(1e2, sd=1e-3))

d2$y <- d2$y * 1e-4


p1 <-
ggplot(d1)+
geom_path(aes(x,y))

# p1 is OK
p1

# p2 is displayed as a horizontal line
p1 %+% d2

with(d2, plot(x, y, t="l"))


Best,

baptiste
